subject: physics
title: Physics equations
welcome_lead: Today's adventure: Physics equations — AQA GCSE Physics (8463) specification, section Appendix A.
meta_desc: GCSE Physics (AQA) practice covering Physics equations, specification section Appendix A.
final_note: You worked through Physics equations — 39 specification statements.

concepts.def: One of the 23 equations in the first Appendix A list. It is not printed on any equation sheet, so a student must write it from memory, substitute values and rearrange it when solving quantitative problems.

The unit the Appendix A equations assume: kilogram for mass, metre for length, second for time, and so on. Values given in grams, centimetres, minutes or hours are converted to SI units before substitution.
The letters HT beside an equation in the left hand column, marking an equation that only Higher Tier papers can require. Foundation Tier papers do not ask for it.
The force acting on a mass because of a gravitational field, found from weight = mass x gravitational field strength (g), W = m g, and measured in newtons.
Energy transferred when a force moves an object along the line of action of that force, given by work done = force x distance, W = F s, measured in joules.
The stiffness of a spring, k in force applied to a spring = spring constant x extension, F = k e. Extension is the increase in length, not the total length.
The turning effect of a force about a pivot, moment of a force = force x distance (normal to direction of force), M = F d, in newton metres.
Force acting normally per unit area of a surface: pressure = (force normal to a surface)/(area of that surface), p = F/A, in pascals.
The rate at which distance is covered, used as distance travelled = speed x time, s = v t, with distance in metres and time in seconds.
The rate of change of velocity, acceleration = (change in velocity)/(time taken), a = (∆v)/(t), measured in metres per second squared.
The single force equivalent to all the forces on an object. Only the resultant force is used in resultant force = mass x acceleration, F = m a.
A property of a moving object given by momentum = mass x velocity, p = m v, measured in kilogram metres per second. It is a Higher Tier recall equation.
The energy of a moving object, kinetic energy = 0.5 x mass x (speed)^2, E_k = 1/2 m v^2. The speed is squared but the mass is not.
Energy stored by raising a mass in a gravitational field, gravitational potential energy = mass x gravitational field strength (g) x height, E_p = m g h.
The rate of energy transfer, power = (energy transferred)/(time), P = E/t, measured in watts. One watt is one joule per second.
The rate of doing work, power = (work done)/(time), P = W/t. It gives the same value as P = E/t because work done is energy transferred.
The fraction of the energy supplied that is usefully transferred: efficiency = (useful output energy transfer)/(total input energy transfer). It has no unit and cannot exceed 1.
The same ratio expressed using power: efficiency = (useful power output)/(total power input). It is used when powers rather than energies are given.
The speed at which a wave transfers energy, wave speed = frequency x wavelength, v = f λ, with frequency in hertz and wavelength in metres.
The quantity of charge moved by a current in a time, charge flow = current x time, Q = I t, in coulombs.
The opposition of a component to current, appearing in potential difference = current x resistance, V = I R, with resistance in ohms.
The rate of energy transfer in a circuit, power = potential difference x current, P = V I.
Power calculated from current and resistance alone: power = (current)^2 x resistance, P = I^2 R. The current is squared, not the resistance.
Energy found from energy transferred = power x time, E = P t, with power in watts and time in seconds.
Energy found from energy transferred = charge flow x potential difference, E = Q V, with charge in coulombs.
Mass per unit volume, density = (mass)/(volume), ρ = m/V, in kilograms per cubic metre when SI units are used.
One of the 12 equations printed on the Physics equation sheet. It does not have to be recalled, but the right one must be selected and applied correctly.
The HT marking on the equation sheet list, showing which of the printed equations only Higher Tier papers can require.
Pressure due to a column of liquid = height of column x density of liquid x gravitational field strength (g), p = h ρ g. It depends on depth, not on the width of the container.
(final velocity)^2 - (initial velocity)^2 = 2 x acceleration x distance, v^2 - u^2 = 2 a s, used when time is not known.
Force expressed as force = (change in momentum)/(time taken), F = (m ∆v)/(∆t). A longer impact time gives a smaller force for the same change in momentum.
Energy stored in a stretched spring, elastic potential energy = 0.5 x spring constant x (extension)^2, E_e = 1/2 k e^2.
The constant c in change in thermal energy = mass x specific heat capacity x temperature change, ∆E = m c ∆θ: the energy needed to raise one kilogram by one degree.
The time for one complete wave or oscillation, period = (1)/(frequency), measured in seconds.
A ratio found from magnification = (image height)/(object height). Because it is a ratio of two lengths it has no unit.
The quantity B in force on a conductor (at right angles to a magnetic field) carrying a current = magnetic flux density x current x length, F = B I l, measured in tesla.
The constant L in thermal energy for a change of state = mass x specific latent heat, E = m L: the energy to change the state of one kilogram with no temperature change.
The relation (potential difference across primary coil)/(potential difference across secondary coil) = (number of turns in primary coil)/(number of turns in secondary coil), V_p/V_s = n_p/n_s.

For a transformer assumed to be 100% efficient, potential difference across primary coil x current in primary coil = potential difference across secondary coil x current in secondary coil, V_p I_p = V_s I_s.
For gases: pressure x volume = constant, p V = constant, at constant temperature for a fixed mass of gas.

mcqs.q: A question gives a mass of 250 g and a time of 2.0 minutes. Which pair of values should be substituted so that the working is in standard SI units?
options: a mass of 0.25 kg and a time of 120 s
a mass of 250 g and a time of 2 minutes
a mass of 250 kg and a time of 120 s
a mass of 0.25 kg and a time of 2 s
mcqs.explain: 250 g is 0.25 kg and 2.0 minutes is 120 s, the SI units of mass and time.

mcqs.q: In the first Appendix A list, what does HT in the left hand column tell you about an equation?
options: Both tiers need it, but Higher Tier asks more often
It is harder to rearrange than the equations near it
Only Higher Tier papers can require that equation
It is printed for you on the equation sheet
mcqs.explain: HT marks the equations that Foundation Tier papers cannot ask for.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the Appendix A equation for the weight of an object?
options: weight = mass x acceleration of the object
weight = mass x gravitational field strength
weight = mass x field strength x height
mcqs.explain: This is Equation 1, W = m g, with weight in newtons and mass in kilograms.

mcqs.q: A force of 12 N drags a crate 0.50 m along the line of action of the force. How much work is done?
mcqs.explain: work done = force x distance, so W = 12 x 0.50 = 6 J.

mcqs.q: A spring of natural length 30 cm is stretched to 35 cm. The spring constant is 15 N/m. What force is applied to the spring?
mcqs.explain: The extension is 5.0 cm, or 0.05 m, so F = k e = 15 x 0.05 = 0.75 N.

mcqs.q: A spanner turns a nut. Which distance is used in moment of a force = force x distance?
options: the distance from the pivot to wherever the hand grips
the length of the spanner along the line of the force
the distance the nut itself turns through as it tightens
the distance normal to the direction of the force
mcqs.explain: Equation 4 specifies the distance normal to the direction of the force, measured from the pivot.

mcqs.q: A brick rests flat on a table. Which area is A in p = F/A?
options: the area of the face that rests on the table
the total surface area of all six faces of the brick
the surface area of the whole table underneath it
the area of the largest face of the brick
mcqs.explain: A is the area of the one surface the force acts normally on.

mcqs.q: A cyclist travels at a steady 15 m/s for 4.0 s. What distance is travelled?
mcqs.explain: distance travelled = speed x time, so s = 15 x 4.0 = 60 m.

mcqs.q: A car speeds up from 4.0 m/s to 10 m/s in 8.0 s. What is its acceleration?
mcqs.explain: The change in velocity is 6.0 m/s, so a = 6.0/8.0 = 0.75 m/s².

mcqs.q: A box is pushed with a force of 30 N while friction of 12 N acts backwards on it. Which force is used in F = m a?
options: the resultant force, which is 18 N
the 30 N pushing force applied to the box
the 12 N force of friction on its own
the two forces added, giving 42 N
mcqs.explain: F = m a uses the resultant force, here 30 N minus 12 N.

mcqs.q: Which calculation gives the momentum of a trolley of mass 2.0 kg moving at 3.0 m/s?
mcqs.explain: momentum = mass x velocity, so p = m v = 6.0 kg m/s.

mcqs.q: A 1.0 kg mass moves at 4.0 m/s. What is its kinetic energy?
A 2.0 kg bag is carried 5.0 m up a ramp and ends 3.0 m above its starting level. Taking g = 9.8 N/kg, what is the gain in gravitational potential energy?
mcqs.explain: E_p = m g h = 2.0 x 9.8 x 3.0 = 58.8 J, using the vertical height.

mcqs.q: An electric heater transfers 6000 J of energy in 30 s. Which statement about its power is correct?
options: Its power is 180 000 W, from energy times time
Its power is 200 W, from the energy over time
Its power is 0.005 W, from the time over the energy
Its power is 6000 W, the energy transferred

mcqs.q: A motor does 900 J of work in 45 s. What is its power output, and why?
options: 40 500 W, because power is work done times time
0.05 W, because power is time divided by work done
20 W, because power is work done divided by time
900 W, since work done and power are the same
mcqs.explain: P = W/t gives 900/45 = 20 W.

mcqs.q: A motor is supplied with 500 J and usefully transfers 300 J, wasting 200 J. What is its efficiency?
options: 0.6, from the useful 300 J divided by the 500 J input
1.5, from the useful 300 J divided by the wasted 200 J
0.4, from the wasted 200 J divided by the input
1.67, from the 500 J input divided by 300 J
mcqs.explain: efficiency = useful output energy transfer / total input energy transfer.

mcqs.q: A pump has a total power input of 400 W and a useful power output of 250 W. What is its efficiency?
options: 1.6, from the total input divided by the useful output
0.375, from the 150 W wasted power over the input
0.625, from the useful output divided by the total input
150 W, the difference between the two power values
mcqs.explain: efficiency = useful power output / total power input = 250/400.

mcqs.q: A wave has a frequency of 25 Hz and a wavelength of 400 cm. What is its wave speed?
mcqs.explain: The wavelength is 4.00 m, so v = f λ = 25 x 4.00 = 100 m/s.

mcqs.q: A current of 3.0 A flows for 2.0 minutes. What charge flows?
mcqs.explain: Q = I t with the time converted to 120 s gives 3.0 x 120 = 360 C.

mcqs.q: A 6.0 V supply drives a current of 0.50 A through a resistor. What is its resistance?
mcqs.explain: Rearranging V = I R gives R = V/I = 6.0/0.50 = 12 Ω.

mcqs.q: A torch bulb works at 4.5 V and draws a current of 0.20 A. What is its power?
A current of 3.0 A passes through a resistor of resistance 4.0 Ω. Which working gives the power dissipated?
mcqs.explain: P = I² R squares the current before multiplying by the resistance.

mcqs.q: A 2000 W heater is switched on for 5.0 minutes. How much energy is transferred?
mcqs.explain: E = P t with the time as 300 s gives 2000 x 300 = 600 000 J.

mcqs.q: A charge of 8.0 C moves through a potential difference of 12 V. How much energy is transferred?
A block of mass 240 kg has a volume of 0.30 m³. What is its density?
mcqs.explain: density = mass / volume = 240/0.30 = 800 kg/m³.

mcqs.q: How should a student treat the twelve equations in the second Appendix A list?
options: Recall them from memory, as with the first list of equations
Use them only when a question says to use the sheet
Select the right one from the equation sheet and apply it
Learn only the ones that are not marked HT in the list
mcqs.explain: These equations are printed on the Physics equation sheet, so they are selected rather than recalled.

mcqs.q: Which statement about the HT flags on the Physics equation sheet is correct?
options: Higher Tier papers alone can require those equations
Every equation printed on the equation sheet is HT only
They mark the sheet equations that must also be recalled
They mark the equations that contain a square or ratio
mcqs.explain: The flag restricts the tier, not the availability of the sheet.

mcqs.q: A tank 1.2 m tall is filled with water to a depth of 0.40 m. Which values should be used in p = h ρ g?
options: h = 1.2 m, the full height of the tank, with ρ and g
h = 0.40 m, together with the area of the tank base
the volume of the water in the tank, with ρ and g
h = 0.40 m, with the density of the water and g
mcqs.explain: h is the height of liquid above the point, here the 0.40 m depth.

mcqs.q: A car accelerates uniformly from 5.0 m/s to 15 m/s over a distance of 50 m. Which working gives its acceleration?
A car of mass 1200 kg is brought to rest from 20 m/s. A crumple zone increases the collision time from 0.20 s to 0.50 s. Why is the force on the car smaller?
options: The same change in momentum is spread over a longer time
The change in momentum itself is smaller in a longer crash
The crumple zone lowers the mass that has to be stopped
The car's change in velocity is smaller as it deforms
mcqs.explain: F = (m ∆v)/(∆t): m ∆v is fixed by the velocities, so a larger ∆t gives a smaller force.

mcqs.q: A spring with a spring constant of 400 N/m is extended by 0.15 m. How much elastic potential energy is stored?
0.50 kg of water is heated from 20 °C to 80 °C. The specific heat capacity of water is 4200 J/kg °C. Which working gives the thermal energy transferred?
mcqs.explain: ∆E = m c ∆θ uses the 60 °C temperature change.

mcqs.q: A sound wave has a frequency of 250 Hz. What is its period?
options: 250 s, because period and frequency match
0.004 s, since period is 1 over the frequency
500 s, since period is twice the frequency
0.04 s, from 1 divided by only 25 hertz
mcqs.explain: period = 1/frequency = 1/250 = 0.004 s.

mcqs.q: An object 4.0 mm tall produces an image 12 mm tall. What is the magnification?
mcqs.explain: magnification = image height / object height = 12/4.0 = 3, with no unit.

mcqs.q: A wire carries a current through a magnetic field. Which length is l in F = B I l?
options: the whole length of the wire in the circuit
the distance from the magnet to the wire
the length of conductor that is inside the field
the length of the magnet producing the field
mcqs.explain: Only the part of the conductor within the field contributes to the force.

mcqs.q: How much energy is needed to melt 0.25 kg of ice at 0 °C? The specific latent heat of fusion of ice is 334 000 J/kg.
A transformer has 100 turns on the primary coil and 400 turns on the secondary coil. The potential difference across the primary is 20 V. What is the potential difference across the secondary?
options: 80 V, as four times the turns gives four times the pd
5.0 V, because more turns must give a smaller pd
420 V, from adding the turns to the primary pd
20 V, since the pd is the same in both coils
mcqs.explain: V_p/V_s = n_p/n_s gives V_s = 20 x 400/100 = 80 V.

mcqs.q: A transformer is 100% efficient. The primary coil has 230 V and 2.0 A, and the secondary coil has 23 V. What is the current in the secondary coil?
options: 2.0 A, as the current is the same in both
0.20 A, since the current steps down too
46 A, which is 230 x 2.0 divided by 10
mcqs.explain: V_p I_p = V_s I_s gives I_s = 460/23 = 20 A.

mcqs.q: A fixed mass of gas at constant temperature is squeezed into half its original volume. What happens to its pressure?
options: It halves, because pressure follows the volume
It stays the same, since the gas mass is unchanged
It falls to a quarter of its original value
It doubles, because p V remains constant
mcqs.explain: With p V constant, halving the volume must double the pressure.

mcqs.q: A sample has a volume of 500 cm³. What value should be substituted for V in ρ = m/V to give a density in kg/m³?
mcqs.explain: 1 m³ is 1 000 000 cm³, so 500 cm³ is 0.0005 m³.

specSource: AQA GCSE Physics (8463) specification; section Appendix A Physics equations
